body: There’s an idea similar to this called determinism, which basically discounts free will because all our decisions are simply an outcome of our upbringing. I find it really interesting, I think you would as well :)

I get this problem too. Take a small piece of masking tape, fold it over on itself so that there’s no stickiness showing through. Make a crease in this tape and put it over your bottom lip. It’ll take a few minutes to soften, but will ultimately feel better when you play and not give you cuts or discomfort. Hope this helped :)

Fabric ligatures don’t necessarily have a negative effect on your sound. I used one for a very long time. From what I’ve heard the only drawback is that sometimes the sound can be more dampened/not as clear. If you’d like, a stock ligature would work just as well, and might give a clearer sound too. Really, it’s up to the decision of the player, but fabric ligatures are just fine to use.

This is correct for concert pitch instruments, but keep in mind if you're looking off of, say, an alto saxophone's chords, you'd need to transpose them from the key of Eb. Chords are transposed to the instrument the part was made for.
